title: Pepperoni or Margherita
description: The Pizza Guy theme: fifteen seconds of cheerful ad music, a hard cut, then ninety seconds about always arriving when chaos peaks.
stylePrompt: Two-part structure. PART A (0:00–0:15): cheesy commercial pizza jingle — bright major key, clean surf/lounge guitar, snappy snare, cartoon brass stabs, deadpan baritone or unfazed androgynous vocal with zero vibrato, professionally neutral, never "acting," 120 BPM, radio-ad brightness, ends on a sampled doorbell ding. HARD CUT (silence or tape splice). PART B (0:15–~2:00): collapses into minor-key 90s piano ballad — soft upright or grand piano, brushed drums, warm bass, subtle string pad, same deadpan vocal (do not suddenly become emotional — sincerity is accidental), ~72 BPM. Optional very quiet distant laser zaps treated like wind chimes under the ballad. Ends on doorbell ding reversed into a soft piano overtone. Mood: the Pizza Guy theme — chaos is not his department; extra napkins are. Comedy that becomes unexpected sincerity without the singer noticing. Use a deadpan male or unfazed androgynous voice; do not use Rubella for the jingle unless requested as a parody cover.
lyrics:
[Jingle — 15 seconds]
Pepperoni or margherita?
Extra napkins in the bag
You've been out for delivery
Since the world began to lag
Tip is appreciated —
So is silence when you dine!
(doorbell ding)

[Hard Cut]
(tape splice / silence)

[Ballad — Verse 1]
I don't ask about the lasers
I don't clock the purple light
I just ring the bell on time
And leave the crust upright
Every doorway looks the same
When you're holding something warm
I've been out for delivery
Since before the last big storm

[Ballad — Verse 2]
UPS last Tuesday, cable on the third
Spiritual advisor when the HOA preferred
Same shoes, different logo, same exact pace
Chaos peaks — I arrive — I never break the face
Pepperoni or margherita?
You can choose while the sky collapses
Extra napkins in the bag
For the ash and for the lapses

[Ballad — Chorus]
You've been out for delivery
Since the world began to lag
I don't need a reason
I just need the address and the bag
If the neighborhood is ending
Someone still has to bring the food
Pepperoni or margherita?
Neither one will change my mood

[Ballad — Verse 3]
Skeleton union on a fifteen
Laser snakes soft-focus behind
I walk through like a crossing guard
With a receipt you have to sign
They ask me how I stay so calm
I say the crust is fine
Tip is appreciated
So is silence when you dine

[Ballad — Final Chorus]
You've been out for delivery
Since the world began to lag
I don't need a reason
I just need the address and the bag
Walking away from the explosion
Not cool — just on schedule, friend
Pepperoni or margherita?
This is where the song should end

[Outro]
(doorbell ding, reversed)
(piano overtone)
Extra napkins in the bag.
notes:
## Production notes
- **Episode placement:** Episode 3 pizza reveal / laser-snake aftermath; recurring Pizza Guy crossover stinger across episodes; end-credits variant (jingle-only 15s or full ballad). EyeWash Station “Out For Delivery” programming block.
- **Emotional arc:** Jingle is pure gag → hard cut → ballad accidentally sincere about always arriving when chaos peaks → final chorus still deadpan → reversed doorbell. The joke is that the singer never “acts” the emotion.
- **Reference artists:** Beach Boys — *Surfer Girl* (emotionally inverted); elevator music that refuses to acknowledge the building is on fire; 90s soft-rock piano ballads sung by someone who thinks they’re still in a commercial.
- **Runtime target:** ~1:45–2:10 full; 15s jingle-only bumper for end tags.
- **Character:** Pizza Guy (uniform rotation: pizza / UPS / cable / spiritual advisor). Never explains why he’s everywhere.
